item.title: Resist attempts to rig 2027 election, Galadima tells Nigerians
item.description: — Daughter disagrees with him over youths’ voting power By Favour Ulebor, Abuja Elder statesman and public commentator, Alhaji Buba Galadima, has urged Nigerians to resist attempts to manipulate the outcome of the 2027 general election, warning that failure to defend their votes could undermine their democratic rights. Galadima gave the charge on Tuesday while speaking with Vanguard at the sixth edition of the Frontier Discourse Annual Public Lecture Series and Awards, organised by Pacesetter Frontier Magazine at Merit House, Maitama, Abuja. The event was held under the theme, “Barrel to Ballot: The Naturalisation of Violence, Nigeria’s Polity, and its Democratic Circus.” Speaking on the forthcoming election, Galadima urged Nigerians not to surrender their electoral rights or allow political actors to manipulate the outcome of the polls. “They should resist all temptations to rig them out. They should. Or else they become slaves forever,” he said. He also called on older Nigerians to speak up for the younger generation, arguing that despite constituting a significant proportion of the population, young people had not been given sufficient opportunities to influence the country’s political direction. “The most unfortunate thing is the youth who make 54 per cent of the population of the country, they have no voting rights, so they cannot change anything. So us, 46 per cent remaining, should have to make a case for them, should be their voice,” he said. Galadima also questioned the neutrality of key democratic institutions, including the judiciary, National Assembly, security agencies and the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC). He alleged that some of the institutions had failed to demonstrate the independence required to protect the country’s democratic process, accusing them of aligning with the interests of political actors. “The security people are not working for Nigeria. They are working for one transient person. They are supposed to be neutral,” he said. He also criticised INEC, alleging that the electoral umpire was not sufficiently independent. “INEC, which is supposed to be independent. They are more Tinubu than independent. More APC than independent,” he said. However, his daughter, Hon. Zainab Buba Galadima, disagreed with his position on the ability of young Nigerians to influence political outcomes through voting. Zainab, a social change advocate and former councillor in the Abuja Municipal Area Council, said young people must participate actively in elections and other civic processes rather than allow political apathy to weaken their influence. She argued that the numerical strength of young Nigerians could translate into political influence if they became more involved in the democratic process. “I certainly disagree with him. item.title: FG integrates 17bn migration records, close readmission talks with EU
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The Federal Government said it has moved more than 17 billion migration records into an integrated system as part of efforts to automate its migration processes. This was as it said it has closed negotiations with the European Union on a readmission agreement that took about a decade to conclude. Minister of Interior, Hon. Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo, disclosed this on Tuesday at a meeting with the EU Commissioner for Internal Affairs and Migration, Mr Magnus Brunner, and his delegation. The meeting was held ahead of the formal signing of the agreement, according to a statement by the Ministry’s Head of Press and Public Relations, Mrs Mary Ali. Tunji-Ojo said the automation and the integration of identity databases would help the authorities verify the nationality of people being returned to Nigeria more quickly and accurately. He identified three categories of people who may be subject to readmission: those holding valid Nigerian travel documents, those who travelled with documents but later lost or destroyed them, and those who travelled without any identification. He said the government was developing systems to establish the identities of such persons through available national records. The minister added that similar arrangements were already being implemented with the United Kingdom, while discussions were ongoing with the United States to replicate the system. He described the agreement as significant, both for facilitating the return of Nigerians with no legal grounds to remain in EU member states and for promoting a more orderly, dignified and mutually beneficial migration management system. Tunji-Ojo assured the EU delegation that Nigeria would honour every provision of the agreement. He stressed that the government’s position on irregular migration was clear, saying Nigeria does not encourage illegal migration or any abuse of the trust established between countries. According to him, building mutual trust should come before discussions on easing migration procedures, since greater confidence between Nigeria and its international partners would create better conditions for legal migration and cooperation. On border security, the minister called for stronger international collaboration and real-time information sharing, particularly against human trafficking, migrant smuggling and other cross-border crimes. He said individual countries acting alone could not effectively tackle these challenges. He also told the delegation that the government had recorded progress in correctional service reforms, with the number of repeat offenders falling from about 13,000 in 2023 to about 1,600 in the previous year. Brunner described the finalisation of the agreement as a significant development in Nigeria-EU relations, saying it could provide a foundation for cooperation in other areas. item.title: Hold governors accountable over increased allocations, Falae tells Nigerians
item.description: — Says Yoruba must complete eight-year presidential tenure By Dayo Johnson, Akure The Allied Peoples Movement (APM) senatorial candidate for Ondo Central, Hon. Sunday Falae, has urged Nigerians to hold state governors accountable for the management of increased federal allocations, insisting that the funds received by states should translate into visible development. Falae, who spoke in an interview in Akure, Ondo State, said Nigerians had not done enough to demand accountability from governors despite the significant increase in funds accruing to state governments under President Bola Tinubu’s administration. “We are not holding them responsible. The money they are getting does not match the development we are seeing,” he said. He argued that the Federal Government had limited powers to directly hold governors accountable because of the constitutional immunity enjoyed by state chief executives, stressing that citizens must take the lead in demanding explanations for the expenditure of public funds. “What are state governments doing with all the money they are getting? That is the problem,” he said. Citing the Owena-Alade-Idanre road in Ondo State as an example, Falae alleged that the project had been awarded and paid for but remained unconstructed. “That road should have been constructed. The money today, we don’t know where it is. The road was not constructed and it was approved and paid. So the money went to somebody’s pocket,” he alleged. He called for accountability at all levels of government, saying governors, senators and local government chairmen should be made to explain how public funds allocated to their respective jurisdictions were spent. On the 2027 presidential election, the APM candidate said the South-West should complete its eight-year presidential tenure, arguing that the region should retain the presidency for another four years after Tinubu’s first term. Falae said his position was one of the reasons he declined to join the African Democratic Congress (ADC), explaining that he was unwilling to campaign against Tinubu. “I want us as Yorubas to finish eight years in office. Buhari finished his eight years. So the Yoruba man must finish his eight years,” he said. He explained that he eventually joined the APM, the party of Oyo State Governor Seyi Makinde, who is its presidential candidate. According to him, Makinde’s emergence as president would also ensure that a Yoruba person completes the remaining four years of the eight-year tenure. Falae expressed support for Tinubu’s re-election bid but described Makinde as an even stronger option, citing his energy, political antecedents and performance as governor of Oyo State. “Does Tinubu deserve it? Yes. Does Makinde deserve it? Even better. He has the energy, and he has done well in Oyo State,” he said. item.title: Sultan Rashid Abdullah Rashid Al Shene: A Strategic Approach To Long Term Investment
item.description: Investment refers to placing money or resources into assets or businesses with the expectation of making an income, profit or growth on investment. Although investment can be seen as a way to make money quickly through opportunities in the market, a successful investment strategy requires patience, careful planning and consideration of risk. This is a key principle within Rashid Abdullah Al Shene’s investment philosophy. Al Shene is the Founder and CEO of Al Shene Marine Holding and is associated with the seafood, cold chain and maritime industries. These industries require a great deal of coordination, long term planning and adaptability to market changes. Therefore, when considering investment decisions they are not just based on short term financial gains. Looking Beyond Immediate Returns One of the most important factors within long term investments is knowing what is a short-term opportunity and what adds real value to the business. Whilst an investment may look profitable at first, you will begin to see how good it actually is when looking at its long term performance. This will involve looking past the profit potential and considering cashflow, debt, quality management and stable operations. These elements will help to ensure your investment can be sustained. Business leaders must be willing to understand and move on from opportunities that don’t fit the important criteria. Not every market that looks good will be a good investment opportunity to make; especially if you cannot easily measure the risk. Understanding Risk Before Making Decisions Risk management is another key element of investing responsibly. In most circumstances, businesses face unpredictable situations. Factors such as cost of supply, consumer needs, legislation and global competitive markets can affect the business. It makes sense for an investing business to consider these factors. Instead of only considering positive outcomes, an investing business should consider negative outcomes and whether they will be able to handle difficult situations. All of this can be seen within the seafood and maritime industries as Sultan Rashid Abdullah Al Shene has stated. Although this careful planning cannot remove all the uncertainties, it can stop businesses from acting without knowing the potential outcomes. The Importance of Sustainable Growth Investing in businesses will have an impact within the economy. Companies create jobs, build relationships with suppliers and contribute to economic activity. Sustainable investments should look at how a project will affect the surrounding businesses. Building strong relationships with suppliers, creating local jobs and providing a consistent standard of service can help create a sustainable business. Businesses who are aiming for rapid growth could struggle. item.title: Senate passes bill to strengthen CBN regulation of fintechs
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA – The Senate has passed a bill seeking to strengthen the regulatory oversight of major financial technology companies and other non-bank financial institutions in Nigeria. The proposed legislation will empower the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) to designate qualifying financial technology operators and other non-bank institutions as Systemically Important Institutions (SIIs), subjecting them to enhanced regulatory supervision. The bill, SB.959, titled A Bill for an Act to Amend the Banks and Other Financial Institutions Act, No. 5 of 2020, to Provide for the Designation, Registration and Enhanced Supervision of Systemically Important Institutions; and for Other Related Matters, was passed on Tuesday after clause-by-clause consideration at the Committee of the Whole. Its passage followed the presentation of a report by the Chairman of the Senate Committee on Banking, Insurance and Other Financial Institutions, Senator Adetokunbo Abiru (APC, Lagos East). Under the proposed amendment, the CBN will be empowered to identify and designate non-bank financial institutions as systemically important based on factors such as their size, transaction volumes, customer base and interconnectedness with the wider financial system. The legislation also provides for the establishment of an official register of designated institutions and enhanced prudential supervision to address potential risks to Nigeria’s financial stability. It seeks to subject major fintech operators and other qualifying institutions to stricter requirements on regulatory compliance, corporate governance, cybersecurity, technology-risk management and operational resilience. Other key provisions include stress testing, data-integrity assessments, enhanced regulatory reporting and supervisory access to relevant information and operational systems of designated institutions. The bill also seeks to strengthen beneficial ownership disclosure, improve transparency in ownership and control structures, and establish enforcement mechanisms and sanctions for institutions that violate regulatory requirements. Presenting the committee’s report, Abiru said the proposed amendment was designed to address emerging vulnerabilities in Nigeria’s financial services sector, particularly the growing influence of large technology-driven financial service providers whose operations had become increasingly interconnected with traditional banking institutions. He said the legislation would strengthen the CBN’s capacity to monitor risks arising from digital financial services, technological disruptions and operational failures that could have wider implications for the financial system. Abiru disclosed that the proposed amendment received broad support from regulatory authorities, government agencies, financial institutions and professional bodies during a public hearing conducted on March 4, 2026. item.title: Police arrest two suspected drug dealers in Bauchi
item.description: By Christopher Ameh, Bauchi The Bauchi State Police Command has arrested two suspected drug dealers and recovered various illicit substances, including Tramadol, Indian hemp and other suspected hard drugs, during a raid in the Yelwa area of Bauchi metropolis. The suspects, identified as Yunusa Iliya, 38, of Yalwan Kagadama, and Emmanuel Linus, 20, of Yalwan Tsakani, were reportedly arrested while allegedly selling illicit substances to customers at Ambassador Area of Yelwa on November 9, 2026. The Police Public Relations Officer, SP Nafiu Habib, disclosed this in a statement, saying operatives of the Violent Crimes Response Unit (VCRU) carried out the operation following credible intelligence. According to him, the operatives recovered 11 sachets and 46 pieces of Tramadol, 10 pieces of Kolos, 61 white tablets and 41 Yellow Boys from the first suspect. He said five capsules of Tramadol 100mg, 230 tablets of Exol and 11 Yellow Boys were recovered from the second suspect. Habib said the arrests reflected the command’s sustained efforts to rid the state of illicit drugs and criminal activities. He recalled that within the preceding 20 days, operatives of the unit had arrested six suspected drug dealers in five separate operations, recovering large quantities of different illicit substances. The police spokesman added that investigation into the latest arrests was ongoing and that the suspects would be charged to court upon its conclusion. Meanwhile, the Commissioner of Police, CP Sani-Omolori Aliyu, commended the operatives for their professionalism, vigilance and prompt response to intelligence. Aliyu warned drug dealers and other criminal elements to desist from their activities, stressing that the command would sustain its operations against illicit drugs and other forms of criminality across the state. He urged residents to provide the police with timely and credible information that could assist in identifying criminal hideouts and preventing crime. The commissioner assured residents that the command remained committed to protecting lives and property, adding that cooperation between the police and the public was essential to maintaining security in Bauchi State. item.title: Cross River sacked LG workers reject reinstatement claim, protest
item.description: By Ike Uchechukwu CALABAR Thousands of aggrieved local government workers in Cross River State on Tuesday protested at the Federal Secretariat in Calabar, rejecting the state government’s claim that 3,000 of them had been reinstated and describing the announcement as a “huge hoax”. The protesters, who also visited the Local Government Service Commission, said they had remained without salaries for months despite working in various local government departments, health centres and revenue units across the state. They lamented that prolonged non-payment of salaries had left many of them sick and struggling to meet their basic needs. The protest followed a recent statement by Governor Bassey Otu, issued through his Chief Press Secretary, Linus Obogo, announcing that 3,000 local government workers had been reabsorbed and would be returned to the payroll. Speaking with journalists during the protest, the group’s leader, Mr Julius Uchi, disputed the announcement, insisting that the affected workers had not been reinstated. “We were not among the people they claimed have been reabsorbed. That information is totally false,” Uchi said. Uchi, who said he was employed in 2025 and posted to the Youth and Sports Department of Obudu Local Government Council, said the affected workers had yet to receive any salaries, prompting them to resume protests. He said the workers did not receive any official communication from the government on the purported reinstatement, adding that they only learnt about it through social media following the governor’s press statement. Uchi said the workers had embarked on several protests over their employment status, leading to the establishment of a commission and subsequently a panel of inquiry before the government eventually issued a notice nullifying the recruitment exercise. He questioned the governor’s reference to reinstatement, arguing that the affected workers were never placed on the payroll in the first place. “When the governor talked about reinstatement, we didn’t understand, because nobody was removed from the payroll in the first place. Salaries have been paid to others, but we have received nothing,” he said. He maintained that the workers were duly recruited after undergoing screening, document verification and clearance by their respective local government councils and the Local Government Service Commission. According to him, their records were also captured by the Auditor-General before they were deployed to their respective duty posts. “We went through the same process others went through, and they were placed on payroll. Some of us even started working before those people,” he said. Uchi added that the affected workers had continued to discharge their duties, including providing services in health centres and revenue-generating departments. “None of us passed through the back door, none of us paid a kobo to anyone, and we were not illegally employed. item.title: Financial inclusion key to Tinubu’s $1trn GDP target – Presidency
item.description: ‎. –1,000 business leaders to sign pact on policy reforms, enterprise growth at Blueprint Summit 2.0 December 3 ‎–As Gaye seeks 50-year African businesses, unveils digital platform ‎ By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ‎ABUJA –THE Presidency on Tuesday, said Nigeria’s ambition of building a $1 trillion economy by 2030 depends largely on bringing millions of economically active Nigerians, particularly women, youths and small business owners, into the formal financial system. ‎The Presidency also noted that to unlock the $1 trillion future by 2030, Nigeria must urgently formalize its grassroots economy, maintaining that bringing millions of women, youth, and small business owners into the formal financial system is no longer optional but a prerequisite for growth. ‎Technical Adviser to the President on Economic and Financial Inclusion, Dr Nurudeen Abubakar Zauro, stated this in Abuja while announcing a partnership between the Presidential Committee on Economic and Financial Inclusion (PreCEFI) and the Africa CEO Club ahead of the Africa Blueprint Summit 2.0 billed to hold on December 3, 2026. ‎Zauro said financial inclusion must go beyond opening bank accounts to providing individuals and businesses with access to credit, savings, insurance, pensions, investment opportunities and wider markets. ‎He maintained that the Federal Government’s economic transformation agenda could not achieve its full potential while significant segments of the population remained excluded from formal financial services and productive economic activities. ‎According to him, financial inclusion is a critical driver of economic growth, enterprise development, job creation and national prosperity. ‎According to him: “This work sits at the heart of the Federal Government’s economic agenda. Millions of our citizens, many of them women, young people, rural households ‎and small business owners, still operate outside the formal financial system. ‎”They lack access to savings, credit, insurance and pensions. If we are to build a one trillion dollar economy, we cannot leave them behind. Inclusion is not ‎charity. It is growth.” ‎The presidential aide said PreCEFI, under the leadership of Vice President Kashim Shettima, was coordinating government institutions, regulators and private-sector stakeholders to expand financial access and ensure that no economically active Nigerian was left behind. ‎Zauro identified digital public infrastructure, consumer protection and simplified onboarding procedures as essential to removing barriers to financial services, particularly the challenges of formal identification and inadequate banking facilities. ‎He stressed that financial inclusion must translate into productive activities, including business expansion, agricultural financing, employment generation and access to domestic and international markets. ‎”Opening an account is the first step, not the last. item.title: HURIWA urges Otti to pay 4,700 teachers
item.description: …Raises concerns over unpaid allowances, rural teachers’ welfare By Chioma Obinna The Human Rights Writers Association of Nigeria (HURIWA) has called on Abia State Governor, Alex Otti, to pay 4,700 newly recruited primary school teachers allegedly working without salaries. The association described the reported delay as unfair to the teachers, who it said were recruited and deployed to public schools, particularly in rural communities, but had yet to receive their first salaries since resuming duties last month. In a statement on Tuesday, HURIWA’s National Coordinator, Comrade Emmanuel Nnadozie Onwubiko, criticised reports that the teachers might not be paid until January 2027 because of a three-month probationary period. “Governor Otti must explain why 4,700 teachers employed by his government should work for months without salaries. These are not volunteering or charity workers. They are employees who deserve to be paid for their services. Probation must not become a licence for exploitation,” the group said. HURIWA also alleged that the teachers’ training allowances had remained unpaid since September, questioning how they were expected to cover transportation costs and meet their family responsibilities without income. The association further asked the state government to explain why the newly recruited teachers were allegedly excluded from the N1 billion reportedly released for teachers during the 2026 World Teachers’ Day celebration. It said the affected teachers claimed that existing teachers received N50,000 each from the fund, while the new recruits were left out. Beyond the alleged non-payment of salaries and allowances, HURIWA raised concerns about the welfare of teachers posted to rural communities, citing inadequate transportation and accommodation, as well as poor school infrastructure. It urged the state government to deploy some of the electric buses reportedly procured by the administration to transport teachers to rural schools, provide affordable accommodation and teachers’ quarters, and rehabilitate dilapidated classrooms. “Governor Otti cannot claim to be transforming Abia’s education sector while the teachers recruited to drive that transformation allegedly beg for transportation money and wait for months to receive their salaries,” the association said. HURIWA demanded the immediate payment of outstanding salaries and allowances, an investigation into the alleged exclusion of the new recruits from the Teachers’ Day payment, and improved welfare and working conditions. “These 4,700 teachers are not volunteers. They are not charity workers. They are employees recruited by the Abia State Government and deployed to serve the state. Governor Otti must pay them, protect their dignity and provide the conditions they need to teach. Government cannot demand their labour and deny them their wages,” it said. item.title: Pochettino open to Man United talks as Carrick’s future hangs in balance
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Mauricio Pochettino would be open to discussing the Manchester United head coach’s position if the club approaches him, as Michael Carrick faces growing uncertainty over his future at Old Trafford. Sky Sports News reports that no final decision has been made on Carrick, while Pochettino is open to talks and could cost United about £7 million to release from his United States contract. United chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox are due to meet minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe on Wednesday to review the season and discuss their recommendations on Carrick. The club is also assessing possible alternatives. Carrick’s position has come under pressure after United went eight consecutive Premier League matches without a win. The team’s late fightbacks in recent matches have offered some encouragement, but have not eased doubts about its overall form. Pochettino, who previously managed Tottenham, Chelsea and Paris Saint-Germain, recently extended his contract as US head coach through 2030. United have considered him for the Old Trafford job before, but there have been no substantive talks with potential replacements so far. United are expected to use the international break to assess the season before deciding their next step. Carrick remains in charge for now, with the club’s leadership weighing whether a change of coach would address the team’s struggles. item.title: Amaechi Accuses APC Of Dodging Policy Debate, Focusing On Opposition
item.description: The vice-presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Rotimi Amaechi, has accused the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) of concentrating on opposition figures rather than presenting its policies and plans to Nigerians ahead of the 2027 general election. Amaechi, a former governor of Rivers State and minister of transportation, said the ruling party was more interested in weakening the opposition than engaging Nigerians on critical national issues. He made the remarks during an interview on Channels Television’s Sunrise Daily on Tuesday. According to him, the APC’s campaign rallies have largely focused on attacking opposition figures, particularly him, rather than addressing issues affecting the country. “The party in power is trying to look for how to weaken the opposition; they are scared. Don’t you see their campaign? Tell me one state they have campaigned in that is not about Amaechi; it’s all Amaechi, Amaechi, Amaechi, Ebonyi, Rivers, Amaechi,” he said. ﻿ Policy Debate Amaechi contrasted the ruling party’s approach with the opposition’s campaign, saying his party had focused on issues such as the economy, social housing and security. “When we were campaigning, we were addressing issues. We addressed the issues of economy, social housing, security,” the ex-minister said. Tinubu speaking at a state reception held in his honour at the newly constructed Banquet Hall of ARISE Palm Resort in Uyo, Akwa Ibom State, following the APC rally at the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium, on Friday, November 6, 2026. He further argued that the APC was using his name as a recurring subject at its campaign events instead of explaining what it intended to do if re-elected. “You know what I do every morning? I call my children, [and] I say, ‘You see, your father has achieved so much that he is now the issue in the political discourse of Nigeria.’ NDC is not calling my name because we are in opposition. Anywhere APC is going tomorrow, it’s Amaechi they will mention; they won’t mention what they will do,” he said. View of a market area in Osun State, Nigeria. The former governor also dismissed what he described as the ruling party’s assurances that things would improve in the future, arguing that Nigerians deserved concrete policy proposals rather than promises. “They are not interested; what they are interested in is, ‘don’t worry, things will be better in the future, just put us in power.’ It’s a referendum,” he added. Amaechi contested the ADC presidential primary ahead of the 2027 election but lost to former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar. He is currently Atiku’s running mate on the party’s ticket. item.title: Anthropic Targets Valuation Of Up To $1.4 Trillion
item.description: Anthropic plans to raise up to $64 billion in its upcoming initial public offering, the artificial intelligence giant said in a filing Tuesday, putting the company’s total valuation at up to $1.4 trillion. The maker of AI agent Claude said in a filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission that it aims to sell 825 million shares of Class A common stock at a Wall Street debut price estimate of “between $70.00 and $78.00” per share, amounting to $64.3 billion. Anthropic had been expected to raise up to $100 billion in its IPO, which would have made it the largest IPO on record. The stock market debut is being seen as a gauge of how long the AI spending boom lifting the US economy can last. And it comes as Wall Street is busy digesting the impact of the US midterm elections, in which Democrats won majority control of both chambers of Congress and are vowing to put the brakes on President Donald Trump’s agenda. Anthropic has been aiming to hold its initial public offering the week of November 16. This photograph shows the logo of the US artificial intelligence safety and research company Anthropic displayed on a smartphone’s screen in Brussels on June 10, 2026. Photo by NICOLAS TUCAT / AFP On Monday, the company announced it would release updated versions of two of its most powerful AI models, Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2, which it said can perform 30 percent faster than previous versions. Growth has been staggering at the company. Anthropic’s revenue reached $17 billion in the third quarter, up from just $1.4 billion a year earlier, a securities filing showed earlier this month. On Tuesday, the company said its annualized projection, known as the run-rate revenue, “was approximately $81 billion as of October 31, 2026, up $10 billion from September 30.” Estimates in recent months had forecast Anthropic’s valuation at up to a staggering $2 trillion, but the estimates have slipped along with a slide in AI stock prices on Wall Street. Several US media outlets, including The Wall Street Journal and The New York Times on Tuesday estimated the valuation of the company at between $1.3 trillion and $1.4 trillion. item.title: Why an Instagram Following Tracker Can Reveal More Than a Profile’s Follower Count
item.description: A popular Instagram account can attract thousands of followers, but that number rarely tells the whole story. For businesses, content creators, and people researching social media trends, another question can be just as interesting: which accounts does that person choose to follow? Someone may publicly promote fashion, technology, or entertainment while following creators in entirely different fields. A business account may begin following emerging influencers long before announcing a collaboration. A public figure may gradually change the types of accounts appearing on their Following list. These observations can provide useful context, particularly when viewed over time. An Instagram following tracker helps organize changes to the accounts a public Instagram profile follows. Rather than relying on a single snapshot, tools such as Snoopreport record detected follows and unfollows across reporting periods. The results can support social media research, although they cannot explain why someone followed an account or reveal information that Instagram keeps private. Why Follower Counts Don’t Tell the Whole Story Follower numbers are among Instagram’s most visible statistics. They influence how people assess popularity, reach, and sometimes commercial value. Yet having a large audience doesn’t necessarily mean an account has a clearly defined set of interests or strong connections within a particular industry. The Following list offers a different perspective. Consider a technology commentator who starts following several artificial intelligence researchers, software companies, and digital policy organizations. Those additions may suggest topics worth investigating. Similarly, a lifestyle influencer who follows numerous local restaurants might be exploring a new content category. Neither example proves a professional plan or future collaboration. Following someone can reflect curiosity, personal connections, or temporary interest. Still, when researchers compare several observations across time, they may discover changes worth examining further. The Difference Between Following and Followers Before using an Instagram following tracker, it’s important to distinguish two commonly confused terms. Followers are people who subscribe to an account’s updates. Following refers to the accounts that the profile has chosen to follow. For example, a creator may have 40,000 followers while following only 600 accounts. A following tracker focuses on changes within those 600 connections, not on identifying people who recently followed the creator. Instagram allows users to inspect the Following list of an accessible public profile. However, the list doesn’t provide a dependable chronological history of when each connection was added. The order in which accounts appear should not be treated as a reliable record of recent follows. To understand changes, the list needs to be observed across different periods. item.title: What an Instagram Likes Viewer Can Tell Us About the Content People Enjoy
item.description: People reveal different sides of themselves on Instagram. Their profiles may feature carefully selected photographs, polished videos, and short biographies, but their everyday interactions with content can tell another story. A person who rarely posts about travel may regularly like photographs of unfamiliar destinations. A creator known for fashion might engage with technology tutorials, food videos, or sports content. These interactions can suggest topics that attract someone’s attention, even when they don’t appear on the person’s own profile. An Instagram likes viewer can help organize detected likes from public accounts, making it easier to identify recurring content themes rather than examining isolated posts. However, likes are an imperfect signal. They may indicate enjoyment, curiosity, support, or simply a momentary reaction. Understanding their limitations is essential before drawing conclusions. Why Instagram Likes Are So Interesting A like is one of the simplest interactions on social media. It takes only a moment, but it can reflect many different motivations. Someone might like a photograph because they admire the subject, appreciate the photography, support a friend, or agree with a message. For content creators and marketers, likes also form part of the wider picture of audience engagement. A beauty influencer may notice that certain makeup tutorials attract more engagement than product announcements. A restaurant could discover that behind-the-scenes videos generate stronger reactions than ordinary menu photographs. These observations can guide content decisions, especially when combined with comments, shares, reach, and other performance metrics. But there is an important difference between analyzing engagement on your own posts and studying what a particular public account likes elsewhere. Instagram makes the first task relatively straightforward. The second is more complicated. Can You See What Someone Likes on Instagram? Instagram lets users inspect the likes associated with individual posts they can access. For example, if a public photograph has received likes, its visible engagement information may show which accounts interacted with it. What Instagram doesn’t provide is a single public page listing all the posts another person has liked. The platform removed its old Following Activity tab in 2019. That feature previously offered a window into some activities of accounts people followed. Today, users can still explore publicly visible interactions, but building a comprehensive history of another account’s likes is not a standard Instagram feature. This is why an Instagram likes viewer is different from simply opening a photograph and checking its engagement.
